reasons: **Safety comes first, so not everything gets done.** This plan finishes about 70% of the most important work. In return, even the crew members who run hottest stay below the safe body-heat limit, though only barely, so watch for signs of heat stress.
**Two fixed rules shape the day.** No one works outside from 2 to 3 pm because of lightning risk. Dev is new and not yet used to the heat, so he stays off the hardest jobs when it's hot.

**The other options aren't better.** Doing heavy work in the cool morning, or spreading work evenly, gets the same 70% done but runs the crew a little hotter. This plan is the safest of the three for the same amount of work.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
